set.typical_award_size: Chapter 21.03 (as amended by Ordinances 1052 and 1059, 2023; code text dated January 29, 2025 attached to the February 11, 2025 Board item) requires projects of 6 to 10 units to pay an inclusionary housing fee, lets larger projects pay in-lieu fees for fractional units under 0.7 or where site conditions qualify, and sets the fee by Board resolution in the Master Fee Schedule, updated annually by the Residential Construction Cost Index. The December 13, 2022 Board item proposed $30 per square foot based on the Vernazza Wolfe in-lieu fee study. Section 21.03.012(A) lets in-lieu fee monies fund construction, acquisition, rehabilitation, low-interest or equity participation loans, grants, rent subsidies, housing trusts and down payment assistance, and provide reasonable reimbursement to the County for infrastructure costs of impact fee waivers granted to 100% affordable developments. Fund balance and any waiver approvals are not published. Before 2023, developers voluntarily paid $4,500 per unit under development agreements.
set.affordability_requirement: Fund uses limited to extremely low, very low, low and moderate income housing (up to 120% AMI); impact fee waiver reimbursement applies only to 100% affordable developments.
eligible_project_detail: 100% affordable rental or ownership developments in unincorporated San Benito County (impact fee waiver reimbursement)
construction, acquisition, rehabilitation, at-risk preservation, loans and grants from in-lieu fee proceeds (Section 21.03.012)
set.cycle_notes: Section 21.03.012(B) requires the County, at least once a year when it holds unappropriated in-lieu fees, to publish a notice of funding availability inviting proposals; the Director recommends, the Planning Commission reviews, and the Board approves awards. Impact fee waivers are requested with the entitlement application. On February 11, 2025 the Board reviewed Chapter 21.03, gave staff direction and formed a Housing Policy Reform Ad-Hoc Committee, so further amendments are possible.
set.next_deadline: No County in-lieu fund notice of funding availability was found as of November 10, 2026. Request an impact fee waiver with the entitlement application and confirm the in-lieu fund balance with Planning and Building.

Resolution 2023-02 and the January 17, 2023 adoption date were not re-read; the current fee amount in the Master Fee Schedule was not opened.

set.typical_award_size: Standard state welfare exemption (Rev. and Tax. Code 214(g)) for low-income rental housing owned by a qualifying nonprofit or by a limited partnership whose managing general partner is a nonprofit or eligible LLC, with a BOE Organizational Clearance Certificate (and a Supplemental Clearance Certificate, BOE-277-L1, for limited partnerships). Claims are filed with the San Benito County Assessor on BOE-267 (first filing) or BOE-267-A (annual), with supplemental affidavit BOE-267-L (nonprofit owner) or BOE-267-L1 (limited partnership); BOE-267-H applies to elderly or handicapped housing. BOE-267-L requires a recorded regulatory agreement or deed restriction, use of tax savings to maintain affordability or reduce rents, and either tax credits or government financing or at least 90 percent qualified low-income tenants; BOE-267-L1 requires tax credits or government financing.
set.cycle_notes: Annual claim filing with the County Assessor, not a competitive NOFA: claims are due February 15 each year (next business day at 5:00 p.m. if it falls on a weekend or holiday). For property acquired after the January 1 lien date, file within 90 days of the first day of the month after acquisition or by February 15 of the following year, whichever is earlier.
set.next_deadline: File BOE-267 or BOE-267-A with BOE-267-L or BOE-267-L1 with the Assessor by February 15, 2027 for the 2027-28 roll; late claims receive 90% relief if filed by January 1 of the next year, 85% after that, with tax, penalty and interest capped at $250.

set.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. All for-sale and rental residential projects of 10 or more units must provide 15% of base units (before any density bonus) as on-site inclusionary units: at least 6% very low income, at least 5% very low or low income, and at least 4% very low, low or moderate income (Section 17.36.050). Fractions of 0.25 or more round up. No in-lieu fee option exists; the only alternatives (Section 17.36.060) are affordable rental units inside a for-sale project or acquisition and rehabilitation of existing market-rate units (rehab value at least 25% of pre-rehab value including land, City-approved physical needs assessment, residentially zoned site, applicant-funded relocation). Ordinance 1252 (ZOA 2023-4) adopted August 6, 2024; Housing Element goal of 150 inclusionary units during 2023-2031.
set.affordability_requirement: Inclusionary units sold or rented only to very low, low or moderate income households (up to 120% AMI, San Benito County HCD limits) or to the City or its designee; units must average at least 85% of the square footage of market units with the same bedroom count, match unit type proportions, bedroom ratio, finishes and exterior design, and be dispersed on site with equal access to common areas; buyers and renters screened by the Administrator through an open public process (no private selection). For-sale units: affordable price restricted 30 years under a recorded agreement, resetting on resale, owner occupancy within 60 days and at least 10 months a year, no rental. Rental units: affordable for 55 years under a recorded affordable housing agreement.
set.next_deadline: Applies at entitlement; an affordable housing agreement is required and inclusionary units must be permitted and occupied in proportion to market-rate units in each phase (Section 17.36.050 F). Exempt: ADUs, projects under 10 units, vesting tentative maps and development agreements in effect at the effective date, complete applications with fees paid before that date, and projects exempted by Gov. Code 66474.2, 66498.1 or other state law. Council may adopt guidelines and administration and monitoring fees by resolution (Section 17.36.080).

set.typical_award_size: Requirement-based entitlement, not a subsidy. Local codification of state density bonus law. Ordinance 732 (adopted August 27, 2024; first reading August 13, 2024, to implement AB 1397 and update state density bonus provisions) amended Chapter 16.82 and added Section 16.82.015, which makes the density bonuses and incentives required by Gov. Code 65915 et seq. available on the terms and conditions in state law. Older 2007 sections on qualifying categories, incentives, waivers, parking, land donation and child care remain in the chapter, and Section 16.82.130 defers to state law amendments.
set.affordability_requirement: Per state density bonus law (55-year rental affordability governs); older chapter text still references 30-year affordability for low and very low income bonus units and equity sharing for moderate income for-sale units.
set.layering_notes: Chapter 16.82 was amended by Ordinance 732 in 2024 to track state law; there is no local enhancement beyond state law. Inclusionary units under Chapter 16.80 can be used to qualify for the bonus (Section 16.80.110), which is the main local layering point. Arroyo Grande has no fee waiver ordinance, RDA successor housing fund or NOFA; its tools are the inclusionary trust fund and this chapter, plus County and HASLO resources. Code text read on the zoneomics mirror.

set.typical_award_size: Special revenue fund (Affordable Housing Trust Fund) receiving inclusionary in-lieu fees. Resolution 2023-056 (October 10, 2023) sets in-lieu fees at $25.70 per leasable square foot for apartments, $14.60 per saleable square foot for townhomes and condominiums and $16.80 per saleable square foot for single family detached, adjusted annually; in-lieu fees may satisfy the requirement for fractional units and ownership developments. Resolution 2023-057 sets the nonresidential linkage fee at $0 per square foot for all nonresidential uses. Fund balance not published in the documents opened.
set.affordability_requirement: Fund money must be spent on activities prioritizing construction of affordable housing in Thousand Oaks for extremely low, very low, lower and moderate income households; preservation or rehabilitation only where there is limited opportunity for new construction (Sec. 9-10.203(a) as amended by Ord. 1719-NS). Assisted units are subject to an Affordable Housing Agreement; Council may adopt fund guidelines by resolution.
set.next_deadline: No City NOFA or fund guidelines found as of November 10, 2026. The 2025 Housing Element APR (March 10, 2026) says the County administers the City's HOME and PLHA funds and that the City expects developers to request funding in 2026. Contact Community Development.
set.layering_notes: Revenue has been thin; the in-lieu fee was reset by Resolution 2023-056 (rescinding Resolution 2012-071) with Ordinance 1719-NS, effective November 24, 2023, and the linkage fee is $0. The City has used land instead: it donated Hillcrest area land to the Housing Land Trust Ventura County for a 78-unit for-sale townhome project with People's Self-Help Housing, provided City land for a navigation center, and partnered with the County on Step Up (77 extremely low income PSH units). A PLHA grant went to HTFVC as Local Housing Trust Fund match in FY 2021-22. For rental gap, look first to the County PLHA plan (which covers Thousand Oaks), the County HOME Consortium and HTFVC.

set.typical_award_size: Deferral, not a waiver: a developer that has not yet paid City development impact fees may defer them from building permit to certificate of occupancy, paying interest at the current five-year Treasury rate. Applies only to the City's own impact fees (13 active fees), not planning or building permit fees, school, Quimby (CRPD) or fire district fees. Dollar value depends on project fee load (staff noted larger projects can reach $5.0 million in City impact fees).
set.affordability_requirement: None; the October 10, 2023 program is open to any development project, not limited to affordable housing. Housing Element Program 7 separately calls for fee deferrals for affordable projects.
set.cycle_notes: Council authorized staff on October 10, 2023 to implement a temporary program by staff report (not by resolution); the staff report says it would expire after one year. A March 19, 2024 Council item approved a deferral for one project under the program. The 2024 APR (March 25, 2025) describes it as in effect until a date uncertain, while the 2025 APR omits it, and no extension item was found in Council or Planning Commission agendas from 2023 to 2026. State law (Gov. Code 66007) separately defers most residential impact fees to final inspection or certificate of occupancy.
set.next_deadline: Status unconfirmed as of November 10, 2026: the program was set to expire after one year and no extension was found. Confirm with Thousand Oaks Finance or Community Development before underwriting.
set.layering_notes: Improves construction-period cash flow and reduces construction loan interest, but interest is charged on the deferred amount; does not reduce permanent sources needed. School district, park district, fire district and permit processing fees are not covered.
